## IdeaViewTxt v0.1.3

Three things were wrong with the popup: the hotkey left its own characters in the file, paging could skip or repeat a page's worth of text, and the file was decoded with the platform charset on the UI thread. All three are fixed, and the panel's index field now points at something that survives a restart.

## Fixes

### The triple tap no longer types into your file

The listener counted key presses and popped the window on the third, but it never consumed the event — so `/` ×3 in an editor left `///` behind, and there was no modifier check, which made <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>/</kbd> (comment line) three times a trigger too. Now

- the third press consumes the `KEY_PRESSED`, and the `KEY_TYPED` that follows it is suppressed as well, so nothing reaches the document (a dead key that produces no `KEY_TYPED` clears the flag on release instead of swallowing the next character you type);
- Ctrl / Alt / Meta / AltGr cancel the sequence, while Shift is allowed (some layouts need it to produce the character);
- the popup opens only if a file path has been saved and the file still exists.

### Paging follows the pages it actually rendered

Each page was rendered with a randomly generated line layout, but the cursor was advanced by a *second*, independently generated size — so the first trip to the next page skipped or repeated up to a page's worth of characters — and scrolling back was computed as "two pages back", which is not where the previous page started. The popup now records the start offset and the layout of every page it shows:

- forward moves to `previous start + previous page size`, i.e. exactly where the rendered text ended;
- back re-renders the recorded page with its recorded layout, so the same characters come back;
- the last page stops at the end of the file instead of padding ten empty rows;
- the position written back to the panel is the start of the page that will be shown next, clamped so a stale index from a longer file cannot land past the end.

### Files are decoded properly and read off the UI thread

`String(bytes)` used the platform charset, so on a Chinese Windows install a UTF-8 file came out as mojibake and a GBK file only worked by accident. Reading also happened on the EDT, which froze the IDE for the duration of a large file. Content now loads through `FileContentLoader`:

- a byte order mark wins (UTF-8 / UTF-16LE / UTF-16BE, and the BOM is dropped);
- otherwise strict UTF-8 is tried, then GB18030 (a superset of GBK, so old Chinese files decode);
- if both fail, lenient UTF-8 keeps the readable characters and shows `U+FFFD` for the broken bytes;
- the read runs on a pooled thread and the result is applied on the EDT.

### One registration for the project service

`FileStateService` carried both `@Service` and a `<projectService>` entry in `plugin.xml`. It is now registered only through `plugin.xml`, which is what the IDE asks for, and the class documents it so the annotation does not come back.

### Listener bookkeeping

Listeners were removed by taking `keyListeners.lastOrNull { it is KeyAdapter }` off the editor component — which could remove another plugin's adapter, or nothing at all. Each editor's adapters are now kept in an identity map and detached precisely, twice-created editors do not stack listeners, and a `FocusAdapter` resets the press count when focus leaves the editor.

## Notes

- Built against IntelliJ IDEA 2024.1.7, `sinceBuild = 241`, so it loads in 2024.1 and later (any edition that ships the platform modules it depends on — `com.intellij.modules.platform` only).
- Settings are per project, in `.idea/viewTxt.xml`: file path, trigger key, starting index, popup width and height. Deleting that file resets the panel.
- The triple tap is a plain-key sequence on purpose: a single keystroke cannot be bound without stealing it from typing, and a modifier combination would have to fight the IDE's own keymap. The counter resets after two seconds of inactivity or when focus leaves the editor.
- Stack: Kotlin 2.1 · IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin 2.10 · Gradle 9 · Java 17 bytecode.
